headline: A reward-free teacher repair improves agentic on-policy distillation on three text-agent benchmarks
summary: Zhao and Yu introduce Rollout-to-Scorer Distillation (R2S), which uses selected teacher takeovers from high-disagreement states of an untrained student to fine-tune the teacher’s token-level scorer before ordinary on-policy distillation (OPD). The student still trains against the frozen scorer with the standard sampled reverse-KL objective; task reward is not used to train it. Across ALFWorld, WebShop and ScienceWorld, the authors report that R2S outperformed three recent agentic-OPD baselines in all twelve model/student/environment cells, averaging 12.8 success points above the strongest baseline in each cell; Appendix E reports that R2S exceeds every baseline in mean on all 24 evaluation splits. The study uses two Qwen teacher families and four students. These are preprint-author results, not independently reproduced; the main table uses one training run per cell and the repair requires up to 19,200 teacher takeover episodes.
